why_this_record: the acquisition path changed after a licence problem; the design is unchanged

source_rejected.loader_script_line: _LICENSE = ""  # TODO: Add the licence for the dataset here if you can find it
source_rejected.why_rejected: the loader script leaves the licence empty while the README tag claims MIT, so MIT cannot be traced from primary information. Same structure as the AIME problem: a redistributor's tag does not replace the rights holder's grant

source_used.why: the authors' own repository github.com/hendrycks/math links to this dataset as the download location for MATH in its README
source_used.note: the Berkeley tarball URL in older references returns HTTP 403, so the authors' current link was used
source_used.split: the source ships a single split of 12500; train/test was reconstructed

equivalence_check.method: sha256 of the whitespace-normalised problem text
equivalence_check.conclusion: the EleutherAI copy is faithful to the data; it was rejected only because its licence attribution cannot be traced

split_reconstruction.rule: rows come from the licence-clean source; the rejected copy is used only as an index of which problems were train and test

ambiguous_excluded.reason: one problem appears in BOTH EleutherAI splits and twice in the source, so no non-arbitrary assignment exists
ambiguous_excluded.problem_head: The points $(0,0)\,$, $(a,11)\,$, and $(b,37)\,$ are the vertices of an equilateral triang

how_the_duplicate_was_caught.check: row counts were reconciled against the source: the two reconstructed splits plus anything excluded must sum to the 12500 rows of the licence-clean source
how_the_duplicate_was_caught.what_it_caught: the first reconstruction produced train 7501 and test 5001, which sums to 12502 and therefore could not be right
how_the_duplicate_was_caught.why_it_matters: without the count check, the same problem would have sat in both splits and the run would have proceeded silently

incidental_finding_train_test_overlap.finding: in EleutherAI/hendrycks_math, one problem appears in BOTH the train and the test split (once each). The same problem occurs twice in the licence-clean source.
incidental_finding_train_test_overlap.scale: 1 problem out of 12500; small but real
incidental_finding_train_test_overlap.prior_report: The literature lead is checking whether this is already reported. If it is, the source will be cited. If it is not found, the wording will be 'we found this in our cross-check and could not confirm a prior report' - NOT 'first to find'.

effect_on_our_results.statement: none. Our data come from the licence-clean source and the EleutherAI copy is used only as an index of which problems were train and which were test. The ambiguous problem is excluded from both splits.

why_the_equivalence_check_mattered: checking equivalence separates two claims that would otherwise be confused: the copy is faithful in content, and its licence attribution is untraceable. Without the check, writing only 'we did not use it because the licence is unclear' would leave a reader suspecting the data itself.
FINAL_DECISION: MATH is NOT used. A DMCA takedown notice covers the dataset.

dmca.claim_summary: more than 10,000 of the 12,500 problems are said to match AoPS Alcumus content at 95+ similarity, covering BOTH problem statements and solutions; the notice explicitly extends to derivative datasets
dmca.observed_consequence: hendrycks/competition_math was removed from the Hub, which is why our first load attempt returned DatasetNotFoundError
dmca.why_an_mit_tag_was_not_enough: Hendrycks' MIT licence covers what he holds rights to; AoPS asserts rights in the problems and solutions themselves. The two are compatible, so an MIT tag did not mean the content could be reused.
dmca.data_handling: all copies moved to benchmarks/_dmca_do_not_use/, not deleted; deletion is the PI's decision
dmca.verified_by: literature lead, first-hand in the official takedown-notice repository

three_layers_seen_in_this_case: 1. the HF card said license: mit - a tag only
2. the loader script said _LICENSE = ""  # TODO: Add the licence for the dataset here if you can find it - the redistributor did not know either
3. a third party (AoPS) asserted rights and filed an actual takedown - this was the operative fact
licence_tags_are_not_primary_evidence.rule_for_next_time: check the LICENSE file itself, the rights holder, and any third-party claims, in that order
